metadata.title: Finish What You Start.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro af_bella) - per-beat mp3 durations are MEASURED, never estimated
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon, SHORTEST forms only (Hi / Ola / Hej / Ciao), cycling least-recently-used first. Last seen: Hej (13), Ciao (14), Ola (15), Hi (16). Least recently used is therefore Hej. NOTE: the SPOKEN cold open is fixed by the user's standing instruction to open 'Hi, I'm Om Mali.' - the lexicon governs the Remotion composer chrome only, not B00's narration.
metadata.target_runtime: Under 3:00 BY DESIGN. 434 words against Ep. 15's measured 0.3731 s/word predicts 2:41.9, leaving ~18 s of margin. The words-only model has run +-5-10% with no consistent sign across Ep. 06-16, so the worst observed overshoot (+10.4%) still lands at 2:58.
metadata.purpose: Ep. 17 of the AI in Astronomy & Space Science series, from weekly_stem_videos/ideas.md Astronomy topic 17 (planning a telescope's night). The episode takes the COMBINATORICS as the hinge: a night's orderings are uncountable, so neither real survey searches them. Both instead CHANGE WHAT A MOVE IS - Rubin shrinks it to 'now', ZTF shrinks it to 'which block' - and the episode measures what that second choice buys.
metadata.boundary: ideas.md Notes: 'Ep. 17 is about planning the survey's own observing schedule, not deciding which transients deserve follow-up (Ep. 10).' Nothing in this episode ranks an alert, scores a candidate, or decides what is worth chasing. Every decision here is made BEFORE the data exists, about where to point. B02 says so.
metadata.color_semantics: Claude fidelity palette. Terracotta #D97757 is THE PLANNER - the thing being examined - and ink #3D3929 is GREEDY, the fixed reference it is measured against. That mapping holds in tour.png, completion.png and airmass.png without flipping, so B06 teaches it once. Two local exceptions, both taught in-beat: in window.png terracotta marks the three highlighted fields (no scheduler exists yet at B03); in bonus.png the terracotta CURVE is greedy-under-payment, and marker fill is the price - filled = exposure rate held, hollow = rate given up. Accented text is #A44A32; #B9B4A0 is strokes and fills only, never text.
metadata.distinct_from_earlier_episodes: Ep. 10 (asteroid/transient follow-up) decides which DETECTIONS deserve telescope time after the fact. Ep. 17 decides where to point before any photon arrives, and never ranks a candidate. Ep. 16 (predictive AO) is a control loop inside one exposure; this is the allocation of thousands of exposures across a night. No plate, number or source is shared with either.
metadata.note: The episode's claim is falsifiable and the falsification test SHIPS as beat B09: greedy is paid, by a tunable bonus, to care about finishing pairs. It climbs to 0.975 - which complicates the story and is stated on screen rather than omitted.

assets.plate_rule: plates carry IMAGERY ONLY - no text, ticks or legend. Every label is placed by scenes.py OUTSIDE the plate, because GATE B is nearly blind to a plate's interior.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Om Mali. This video is about how a survey telescope decides what to point at next, and why the two biggest sky surveys both solved that without machine learning.

show.event: the composer types the ask on the cream stage
the send button arms in terracotta
running indicator: enumerating orderings of one night
three result lines land in order

props.command: A survey telescope takes a few thousand exposures a night, and the order decides how deep the survey gets. Nobody can search those orders. So what do the real schedulers do instead?
props.runningText: counting the orderings of a 1000-exposure night...
output: 1000 exposures order 10^2567 ways - not a search space
Rubin shrinks the MOVE to 'now': best of the whole sky, every 30 s
ZTF shrinks it to 'which half-hour block', then solves that exactly

beats.narration_text: Seventeen episodes on where AI's answers come from. This one is about a problem big enough to look like AI's job, and isn't.

show.event: OM MALI writes in, terracotta hairline underlines it
role line fades in: Humanitarians AI - presenter
a card draws beside it
row one lands and is STRUCK: big enough / to look like AI's job
row two lands boxed: this one / is a constraint, not a guess
series line: Ep. 17

beats.narration_text: Here's the whole idea. A night is a few thousand exposures, and the order decides how deep the survey gets. You cannot search those orders. So both real schedulers change what one move means.

show.event: a card draws on the cream stage
line one types: A NIGHT IS AN ORDER, sub: a few thousand exposures, one sequence
line two: THE ORDERS CANNOT BE SEARCHED, sub: not a big space - no space at all
line three lands in the accent and is UNDERLINED: SO CHANGE WHAT A MOVE IS
closer: where to point, decided before any photon arrives

beats.narration_text: This is the board. Every field is a hill: it rises, it peaks at its own hour, it sets. Below twenty degrees you may not point. Nothing here is a decision yet.

show.event: plate fades up: altitude against time, 34 field tracks
three terracotta tracks brighten - each peaks at a different hour
label OUTSIDE the plate, left: ALTITUDE / right edge: 8 HOURS
the shaded strip is called out: BELOW 20 DEG - CANNOT POINT
closer under the plate: this is the board, not the game

beats.narration_text: Now the decision. A thousand exposures can be ordered more than ten to the two-thousandth ways. Every atom in the universe is ten to the eightieth. Nobody searches this. Nobody ever will.

show.event: 1000 EXPOSURES types on the cream stage
the exponent counts up and settles: 10^2567 ORDERINGS, in terracotta
a ghost rule drops beneath it: 10^80 ATOMS IN THE UNIVERSE
the gap between the two is bracketed, ink
closer in the accent: NOT A BIG SEARCH. NOT A SEARCH.

beats.narration_text: Rubin shrinks the move to right now. Every thirty seconds it scores the whole sky, slew time, depth, coverage owed, adds them up with weights, and takes the highest. Greedy, on purpose.

show.event: three small sky maps draw in a row, ink: SLEW, DEPTH, COVERAGE OWED
each gets a weight glyph, then they sum into one COMBINED map in terracotta
a single terracotta ring lands on the combined map's brightest cell
a clock chip ticks beside it: EVERY 30 SECONDS
closer: highest reward wins. no lookahead.

beats.narration_text: ZTF shrinks it differently: not which exposure next, but which half-hour block. Sixteen blocks, one filter each. That's small enough to solve exactly, as an integer program. Then you order inside each block.

show.event: a strip of 16 blocks draws across the top, ink
one block lights terracotta - the unit of decision
plate fades up beneath: two alt-az dials, one half-hour each
labels OUTSIDE the plate: left GREEDY (ink), right PLANNER (terracotta) - teaches the colour map
closer: the tour is the easy half. choosing the SET is the hard half.

beats.narration_text: One constraint does the work. A request is a pair: one green exposure and one red. The solver may decline a field entirely. It may not take half a pair. That's an equals sign.

show.event: a pair glyph draws: two chips side by side, g and r
option A lands, ink: TAKE BOTH - allowed
option B lands, ink: TAKE NEITHER - allowed
option C lands and is STRUCK in terracotta: TAKE ONE - forbidden
the constraint types below in mono, accent on the equals: sum_t Y = n_req * Z

beats.narration_text: Here's what that bought. Greedy started four hundred one fields and left seventy-eight unfinished. The planner started three hundred sixty and left none. Half a pair is not half a detection, it's zero.

show.event: plate fades up: two grids, one square per STARTED field
labels OUTSIDE: left GREEDY 401 STARTED, right PLANNER 360 STARTED
a terracotta count lands over the left grid: 78 HOLLOW = STRANDED
over the right grid, ink: 0
closer in the accent: half a pair is zero detections

beats.narration_text: Fair objection: maybe greedy wasn't told to care. So I paid it to finish pairs. It climbs to ninety-eight percent, but by starting fewer fields and giving up rate. It never reaches the line.

show.event: plate fades up: completion against finish-bonus
labels OUTSIDE: x-axis PAID MORE TO FINISH, y-axis COMPLETION
the ghost dashed line is named: THE PLANNER, 1.00
the two hollow markers are called out in terracotta: RATE GIVEN UP
closer: it bought completion by becoming LESS greedy

beats.narration_text: Throughput was never the difference: ninety point five exposures an hour against ninety. What the planner won was depth it never asked for. And it isn't strictly better: ZTF's planner made more filter changes.

show.event: two rate chips land level with each other, ink: 90.5 /h and 90.0 /h
plate fades up beneath: airmass distributions
labels OUTSIDE: LOWER IS DEEPER, median 1.7 ink vs 1.3 terracotta
the honesty card draws, ink: ZTF ILP 3.6 FILTER CHANGES/NIGHT vs GREEDY 2.0
closer: it was told to avoid them. it made more.

beats.narration_text: Notice what never appeared. No network. No reward learned from experience. The structure was known, so they encoded it. Learning shows up once, offline, tuning hand-built feature weights. It does not drive the telescope.

show.event: the verdict artifact draws on the cream stage
rows land in order
the last row settles in terracotta

artifactLines: The objective is KNOWN: depth per unit time, written down.
The constraints are KNOWN: horizon, filter, block length.
So encode it and solve it. Don't learn it.
Learning appears once, offline, tuning hand-built feature weights (Naghib+ 2019).
What drives Rubin on the night: a weighted sum, chosen greedily, every 30 seconds.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take a schedule you actually run, a week, a build queue. Write down the thing that must finish, not the thing you count. Then ask whether your rule can see it.

show.event: the composer types the handoff ask
the send button arms in terracotta
two prompt lines land

props.command: Take one schedule you actually run. Name the unit that only counts when it is COMPLETE - not the unit you report. Then check whether your scheduling rule can even see that unit.
props.runningText: checking whether the rule can see a half-finished thing...
output: if it cannot, no amount of tuning will make it finish them
if it can, you have a constraint - not a preference
